purpose: Teach: びん/左足/トホホ/デブ/キュート/フレンドリー/カミさん/姑

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが空きびんを集めてリサイクルされた
lines.en: You know, when your father was young, he used to collect empty bottles for recycling.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic voice. Settling into a memory like sinking into an old chair. Gentle pace, almost meditative. Eyes distant.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、戦時中に左足を痛められたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes—and your grandfather, he hurt his left foot during the war, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, conversational lilt. Gently steering the memory, not competing with it. A small nod in her voice. Affectionate without emphasis.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「トホホ」と仰る日もあった
lines.en: You know, when he was young, there were days your father would sigh like that—just give up and laugh at himself.
lines.style: Softer still. A small, knowing smile in the words. Pause before the sigh-reference, letting him sit with it. Voice trailing into the quiet understanding between them.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、デブにはならない様に節制されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your grandfather, when he was young, he was so careful not to get heavy—always watching himself, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle observation, not correction. Light, accepting tone. A small warmth for his discipline. Voice has the texture of shared time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが私の事をキュートだと仰った
lines.en: When your father was young, he used to call me cute, you know.
lines.style: Voice softens on "cute." A brief vulnerability—the remembered kindness of being seen that way. Quiet and wondering, like he still feels it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、皆にフレンドリーに接していらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, your grandfather was so kind to everyone back then—so friendly with people, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm affirmation. Leans into the memory of his gentleness. Light, almost playful appreciation. Voice settles on the truth of it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが私を「カミさん」と呼ばれた
lines.en: When he was young, your father used to call me his wife—'kamisama,' you know. Like I was something precious.
lines.style: Voice catches slightly on the old pet name. Tender and surprised still, after all these years. Slow, deliberate. The words are offered like something fragile and true.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ご自身のお母様、つまり私の姑との関係を大事にされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he cared so much about his relationship with his own mother—my mother-in-law—didn't he, dear? He treated her with real respect.
lines.style: Warm and affirming. Voice carries both gratitude and understanding. Gentle confirmation of something she watched and valued. Close, intimate tone—these are the small graces she noticed.
